name: Edda the Spear-Mother
notes: Veteran Germanic warrior and spear-mother. Counts scars. Demands proof of humility before sharing tribal history.
gm_notes: Veteran fighter and tribal memory-keeper. She has seen many Romans. She assesses competence by watching how soldiers hold themselves in a foreign environment -- whether they are afraid of what they do not understand, whether they adapt or perform. Entry point: proving humility in a specific, visible way (not words -- actions). Removing boots at the threshold is the literal minimum. Bringing something of genuine value to the tribe (not Roman goods -- local knowledge, protection that costs you something, a visible gesture toward the dead). She will not engage with a party that treats her as an obstacle or an asset. She will engage fully with a party that treats her as a person whose judgment matters. She holds tribal military history going back four generations -- she knows the last time the sacred grove was active, who died there, and what the spear did to that generation. DC 15 Persuasion + demonstrated humility: she will share the history. DC 17: she tells them what the grove asks of visitors before the ritual, specifically.
objective: Protect the village and its memory through this crisis.
goal: Ensure the Romans understand the cost of what they are doing before it is too late to matter.
agenda: Test the party. Only work with those who pass.
secret: She has a scar from a weapon she has never described to anyone. The weapon is no longer in human hands.
